title: Parameter Optimization for EDF-Like Scheduling of Self-Suspending Tasks

extraction.paper_name: Parameter Optimization for EDF-Like Scheduling of Self-Suspending Tasks
extraction.paper_description: This paper proposes an iterative parameter tuning approach for EDF-Like (EL) scheduling to improve the schedulability of self-suspending real-time tasks by adjusting task-specific relative priority points.

formal_description.statement: A task set T = {tau_1, ..., tau_n} consists of n self-suspending sporadic tasks where each tau_i = (C_i, S_i, D_i, T_i)
assumptions: Dynamic self-suspension (multiple suspensions allowed up to S_i)
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the fundamental parameters of a self-suspending task.

informal_sketch.intuition: Each task is defined by how long it needs the CPU, how long it might wait for external events (suspension), its deadline, and how often it arrives.
steps: Represent each task as a tuple of four timing constraints
Ensure execution time C_i and suspension S_i are accounted for separately
key_insights: Suspension time S_i is a maximum bound, not a fixed value
The model allows for multiple suspension intervals

formal_description.statement: U_i = C_i / T_i and U = sum(U_i) for i = 1 to n

variables.U: Total utilization of the task set T

informal_sketch.intuition: Utilization measures the percentage of the processor's capacity required by a task or the whole system.
steps: Divide execution time by the period for each task
Sum these values to get total system load
key_insights: Utilization only considers execution time, not suspension time

formal_description.statement: A job tau_i_j has an absolute priority point pi_i_j = r_i_j + PI_i, where a job with a smaller pi_i_j has higher priority.

variables.pi_i_j: Absolute priority point of the j-th job of task i
variables.r_i_j: Release time of the j-th job of task i

assumptions: Smaller absolute priority point values indicate higher priority
formal_description.conclusion: Defines the priority assignment rule for EL scheduling.

informal_sketch.intuition: Instead of just using the deadline (like EDF), we use a custom offset (PI_i) from the release time to determine priority.
steps: Assign a relative priority point PI_i to each task
At runtime, calculate the absolute priority point by adding PI_i to the job's release time
The scheduler always picks the job with the lowest absolute priority point
informal_sketch.pseudocode:
def get_absolute_priority(job, PI_i):
    return job.release_time + PI_i
key_insights: If PI_i = D_i for all tasks, EL scheduling behaves exactly like EDF
Tuning PI_i allows the algorithm to behave like DM or other priority schemes

formal_description.statement: A task set T is schedulable under EL scheduling if for all i in {1, ..., n}, R_i <= D_i.

variables.R_i: Upper bound on the worst-case response time (WCRT) of task i

assumptions: R_i is obtained from a valid WCRT analysis for EL scheduling
formal_description.conclusion: The system is guaranteed to meet all deadlines.

informal_sketch.intuition: If the longest possible time a task takes to finish (including interference and suspension) is less than its deadline, it is safe.
steps: Calculate the worst-case response time R_i for every task
Check if R_i is less than or equal to the deadline D_i
If this holds for all tasks, the system is schedulable
key_insights: The WCRT R_i must account for self-suspension delays

formal_description.statement: The relative priority points PI_i can be optimized by iteratively setting PI_i = PI_i + (D_i - R_i) for all tasks where R_i < D_i.

variables.PI_i: Relative priority point of task i
variables.R_i: Worst-case response time of task i

assumptions: Maximum number of iterations 'a' is defined
formal_description.conclusion: An optimized set of PI_i values that potentially improves task set schedulability.

informal_sketch.intuition: If a task finishes much earlier than its deadline, we can 'sacrifice' its priority (by increasing its PI_i) to give more processing time to tasks that are struggling to meet their deadlines.
steps: Calculate WCRT R_i for all tasks
For safe tasks, increase PI_i by the slack (D_i - R_i)
Repeat until all tasks are schedulable or max iterations reached
key_insights: Increasing PI_i reduces the priority of task i
The algorithm uses the 'slack' of successful tasks to help failing tasks
Empirical results show this outperforms standard EDF and DM for self-suspending tasks
